amenitiesDescription:
The pool deck is the center of the building: a resort-style pool with integrated in-pool lounging steps, a landscaped sun shelf with panoramic views, and an outdoor bar and sink for casual gatherings. Wellness runs alongside it, with a fitness center carrying cardio, strength equipment and free weights, a sauna for heat therapy, and an outdoor yoga lawn for open-air practice.

Indoors, the residents' club room and social lounge carries sculptural lighting, an entertainer's kitchen, and generous seating; a co-working center offers dedicated desks and private booths, with an A/V-ready conference room beside it. The ground plane is built for families: a children's playground, a half basketball court with a court wall, a splash fountain set within the garden, and a dog park. Building services include an intimate arrival lobby with 24-hour concierge, a smart package room with integrated lockbox, dedicated resident and bicycle storage, controlled-access entry, on-site property management, a resident app for amenity reservations and valet coordination, and assigned parking with 24-hour valet.
architect: Asprea Studio with Caymares Martin A&E Design
description: Seventeen Gables is a 117-residence, eight-story condominium at 1715 Douglas Road on the eastern edge of Coral Gables. Developed by Ascendra Capital and BAM Property Development, with design and interiors by New York-based Asprea Studio and Caymares Martin A&E Design as architect of record, it is positioned as attainable luxury in a submarket that produces very little new condominium supply and prices almost all of it well above this. Residences run from one to three bedrooms across 557 to 1,428 square feet, with nine-foot ceilings, floor-to-ceiling impact glass, a balcony with every home, engineered stone counters paired with European-style cabinetry, a Bosch cooking suite with paneled Fisher & Paykel refrigeration and dishwasher, spa-inspired baths with floating vanities, and Blomberg washer-dryers in residence. Released pricing as of June 2026 runs from $634,900 for a 557 square foot one-bedroom to $1,893,900 for the 1,428 square foot three-bedroom, with association dues budgeted at $1.60 per square foot. At eight stories it is among the tallest buildings in the East Gables, with panoramic views spanning the Coral Gables tree canopy to the Miami skyline. The amenity program includes a resort-style pool with in-pool lounging steps and a landscaped sun shelf, a fitness center and sauna, an outdoor yoga lawn, a residents' club room with entertainer's kitchen, a co-working center with private booths and an A/V-ready conference room, plus a half basketball court, children's playground, ground-level splash fountain, and dog park, with 24-hour concierge and valet alongside assigned parking. The project closed a $60 million construction loan from Dwight Mortgage Trust in February 2026, broke ground that May, and is expected to deliver in the first quarter of 2028.
editorialLine: A quieter corner of the Gables, eight stories up.

faq.question: How much do residences at Seventeen Gables cost?
faq.answer: Released pricing as of June 2026 runs from $634,900 for a 557 SF one-bedroom to $1,893,900 for the 1,428 SF three-bedroom with two and a half baths. One-bedrooms are priced from $634,900 to $798,900, one-bedroom-plus-den plans from $820,900, and two-bedrooms from $861,900 to $1,243,900. Across the released sheet that works out to roughly $955 to $1,377 per square foot, averaging about $1,132. Pricing is subject to change without notice.

faq.question: What is the deposit structure at Seventeen Gables?
faq.answer: Forty percent is due before closing, spread across four payments: 10% at contract, 10% at 90 days from contract, 10% at 180 days from contract, and 10% at top-off, with the balance due at closing. That is a gentler schedule than the 20%-at-contract structures typical of Miami's ultra-luxury tier.

faq.question: When will Seventeen Gables be completed?
faq.answer: Estimated completion is the first quarter of 2028. Dwight Mortgage Trust closed a $60 million construction loan in February 2026 and the developers broke ground in May 2026, concurrent with the sales launch rather than after clearing a pre-sale threshold, so the schedule does not depend on absorption.

faq.question: What are the HOA fees at Seventeen Gables?
faq.answer: Association dues are budgeted at $1.60 per square foot, which works out to roughly $891 a month for a 557 SF one-bedroom and about $2,285 a month for the 1,428 SF three-bedroom. Figures are estimates and subject to change.

faq.question: Where is Seventeen Gables located?
faq.answer: At 1715 Douglas Road, at Alhambra Circle and Douglas Road on the eastern edge of Coral Gables. It is within walking distance of downtown Coral Gables dining and shopping, and minutes from Miracle Mile, the Coconut Grove waterfront, the University of Miami, and Brickell.

faq.question: What amenities does Seventeen Gables offer?
faq.answer: A resort-style pool with in-pool lounging steps and a sun shelf, an outdoor bar, a fitness center with cardio and free weights, a sauna, an outdoor yoga lawn, a residents' club room with entertainer's kitchen, a co-working center with private booths and an A/V-ready conference room, a half basketball court, a children's playground, a splash fountain, and a dog park. Services include 24-hour concierge, assigned parking with 24-hour valet, a smart package room, and on-site property management.

investmentThesis:
Coral Gables produces very little new condominium supply, and nearly all of it is aimed at the buyer already living there and moving down from a house. Ponce Park opens at $3.1 million; Cora Merrick Park at $900,000. Seventeen Gables opens at $634,900, below both, which makes it the entry point into new construction in the city and the natural landing spot for Gables renters, University of Miami faculty and staff, and Brickell and Coconut Grove workers who want the address and the school district without a single-family price. The site is on Douglas Road at the eastern boundary, minutes from Miracle Mile, the Grove waterfront, and the Brickell financial district.

The financing is the strongest signal. Dwight Mortgage Trust closed a $60 million construction loan in February 2026 and the developers broke ground in May, concurrent with the sales launch rather than after clearing a pre-sale threshold. That is unusual in a lending market that has grown selective on Miami condominium construction, and it means delivery is not contingent on absorption. BAM Development, founded by Mayer Berkovits, and Ascendra Capital, with David Steinberg as partner and CIO, are self-funding the balance. At 117 residences the building is small enough to sell through without a long absorption tail, and the 10/10/10/10 deposit schedule spreads the pre-closing commitment further than the 20-percent-at-contract structures typical of the ultra-luxury tier.

name: Seventeen Gables
residenceContent: Seven layouts across 557 to 1,428 square feet, from a one-bedroom to a three-bedroom with two and a half baths, with dens available at most sizes. Ceilings run nine feet, walls are floor-to-ceiling impact glass, and every residence has a balcony. At eight stories on the East Gables edge, that outlook runs over the Coral Gables canopy toward the Miami skyline rather than into a neighboring tower. Kitchens pair premium engineered stone counters with European-style cabinetry and a Bosch cooktop and ovens, with the Fisher & Paykel refrigerator and dishwasher paneled to disappear into the millwork. Baths are spa-inspired, with floating vanities and designer fixtures. A Blomberg washer and dryer is integrated in every home, and smart-home control covers lighting and climate.
